item.title: Health Department Reminds Flood Safety Precautions After Heavy Rains
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: The Florida Department of Health in Escambia County is urging residents to take precautions when exposed to floodwaters, particularly as the region faces continued wet weather. While brief skin contact with flood waters typically doesn't pose an immediate health threat, contaminated waters carrying bacteria or dangerous debris can present serious…
item.content:encoded:
The Florida Department of Health in Escambia County is urging residents to take precautions when exposed to floodwaters, particularly as the region faces continued wet weather. While brief skin contact with flood waters typically doesn't pose an immediate health threat, contaminated waters carrying bacteria or dangerous debris can present serious risks to residents.

Health officials recommend avoiding wading through or swimming in floodwaters whenever possible. Waters can carry pathogens, chemicals, and sharp objects that aren't visible to the naked eye. Residents should also wash thoroughly if they do come into contact with flood water, especially before eating or touching their faces.

The health department also advises residents to avoid driving or walking through flooded roadways, as water depth can be deceptive and swift currents dangerous. Floodwaters can also hide hazards like downed power lines or debris beneath the surface. Anyone experiencing symptoms like nausea, vomiting, or persistent skin irritation after flood exposure should contact their healthcare provider.

item.content:encoded:
Westbound traffic on Interstate 10 came to a standstill late Friday morning after a truck towing another commercial vehicle overturned just west of Pine Forest Road, according to North Escambia reporting. The crash happened around 11:55 a.m. in an active highway construction zone, blocking lanes during a busy travel period as Panhandle residents prepared for Hurricane Isaias.

The extent of injuries, the cause of the crash, and how long lanes remained closed were not immediately detailed in initial reports. The incident complicated traffic during what was already expected to be a congested travel day ahead of the approaching storm system.

item.content:encoded:
After recent storm activity, sunshine and calmer conditions are expected to return to the North Escambia area through the weekend, giving residents a chance to tackle cleanup efforts.

Saturday will be partly sunny with highs near 75 degrees, though southwest winds around 15 mph with gusts up to 25 mph may still be noticeable. Saturday night will remain windy as clouds clear out, with lows dropping to around 59 degrees.

Sunday looks even better, with sunny skies and highs climbing to near 84 degrees.

item.title: Escambia County Shifts to Recovery Mode After Hurricane Isaias Landfall
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Escambia County is mobilizing rescue and recovery efforts following Hurricane Isaias, which made landfall near Destin Friday evening, October 9, as a Category 2 storm with sustained winds of 105 mph, according to local reporting. The hurricane crossed the Florida Panhandle at approximately 8:30 p.m. Friday, bringing significant wind and weather…
item.content:encoded:
Escambia County is mobilizing rescue and recovery efforts following Hurricane Isaias, which made landfall near Destin Friday evening, October 9, as a Category 2 storm with sustained winds of 105 mph, according to local reporting.

The hurricane crossed the Florida Panhandle at approximately 8:30 p.m. Friday, bringing significant wind and weather impacts to the region. County officials say public safety remains the top priority as communities begin assessing damage and transitioning from emergency response to longer-term recovery operations.

Residents should expect ongoing efforts from emergency management, public works, and first responders as the county works to clear roads, restore utilities, and address immediate needs in affected areas. Escambia County residents seeking specific recovery information are encouraged to check official county channels and emergency management updates.

item.title: Hurricane Isaias threatens Pensacola area with damaging winds, flooding
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Hurricane Isaias is bearing down on the Pensacola area as of Friday evening, positioned about 45 miles east-northeast of the city with sustained winds of 90 mph, according to multiple weather reports. The storm is moving over the western Florida Panhandle with a northward motion at roughly 20 mph, bringing a significant threat of damaging winds…
item.content:encoded:
Hurricane Isaias is bearing down on the Pensacola area as of Friday evening, positioned about 45 miles east-northeast of the city with sustained winds of 90 mph, according to multiple weather reports. The storm is moving over the western Florida Panhandle with a northward motion at roughly 20 mph, bringing a significant threat of damaging winds and flash flooding spreading inland across the region.

Forecast models indicate Isaias will continue moving north-northeast or northeast through Sunday, keeping the Pensacola area in the path of the hurricane's most dangerous impacts. Residents in Escambia and Santa Rosa counties should prepare for potential power outages, downed trees, and localized flooding as the system moves inland.

Emergency officials urge residents to secure outdoor items, review evacuation plans if in a flood-prone area, and monitor National Weather Service updates for changes to the storm's track or intensity.

item.content:encoded:
Pensacola Regional Airport recorded a significant wind gust early Saturday morning, according to automated weather station data. The National Weather Service ASOS (Automated Surface Observing System) at the airport logged a peak gust of 74 knots — roughly 85 miles per hour — from the north at 2:53 a.m., with sustained winds around 26 knots.

The reading reflects active weather conditions moving through the area. Visibility at the airport was reported at 10 statute miles with broken cloud cover around 2,900 feet and overcast skies at 3,600 feet. Barometric pressure was noted at 29.64 inches.

No immediate reports of damage or flight disruptions were available, but such wind speeds can affect airport operations and ground conditions.

item.title: SS United States to Sink as Artificial Reef off Destin in November
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: The SS United States, a historic ocean liner, is set to be deployed as an artificial reef in the Gulf of Mexico during the second week of November, according to Okaloosa County officials. The vessel will be sunk about 22 nautical miles southwest of Destin-Fort Walton Beach, creating what organizers say will be the world's largest artificial reef.…
item.content:encoded:
The SS United States, a historic ocean liner, is set to be deployed as an artificial reef in the Gulf of Mexico during the second week of November, according to Okaloosa County officials. The vessel will be sunk about 22 nautical miles southwest of Destin-Fort Walton Beach, creating what organizers say will be the world's largest artificial reef.

Okaloosa County commissioners have been coordinating with safety and security partners to ensure a controlled and safe deployment, though officials note the timeline remains weather-dependent and subject to change. The project is part of a broader effort to create an environmental and economic resource for the region's tourism industry.

The SS United States, which operated as a transatlantic passenger liner for decades, has been docked in Philadelphia for years. The effort to turn the vessel into an artificial reef has been in development for some time, with county officials noting they promised the public a 30-day advance notice before deployment — a commitment being met with this announcement.

No immediate information was available on injuries or the full scope of damage across the area. Local emergency management and first responders were monitoring the situation as the system moved through Northwest Florida.

item.title: Boil Water Notice in Effect for Escambia County After Hurricane Isaias
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: The Florida Department of Health in Escambia County is reminding residents to follow boil water precautions after Hurricane Isaias damaged local water systems and prompted several communities to issue boil water notices. The advisory is in place to protect public health by eliminating any harmful bacteria, viruses, or parasites that may have…
item.content:encoded:
The Florida Department of Health in Escambia County is reminding residents to follow boil water precautions after Hurricane Isaias damaged local water systems and prompted several communities to issue boil water notices. The advisory is in place to protect public health by eliminating any harmful bacteria, viruses, or parasites that may have entered the water supply during the storm.

Residents should bring tap water to a rolling boil for at least one minute before using it for drinking, cooking, making ice, brushing teeth, or washing dishes, according to DOH-Escambia. Bottled water is a safe alternative if available. The department also recommends using boiled or bottled water when washing dishes and to be mindful of pets by providing them with boiled or bottled water as well.

The boil water notice will remain in effect until local utilities and the Department of Health notify residents that it is safe to use tap water again. A current list of affected areas is available on the Florida Department of Health's website at floridahealth.gov/environmental-health/drinking-water/boil-water-notices. Residents with questions can contact the State Assistance Information Line at 1-800-342-3557.

item.title: Hurricane Isaias Expected to Make Landfall This Evening; 72 mph Winds Already Battering Gulf Coast
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Hurricane Isaias is moving toward landfall this evening along the Gulf Coast, with tropical storm-force winds already lashing the region, according to the National Hurricane Center. The NHC reported a 72 mph gust at Orange Beach, Alabama on Friday evening, giving a preview of what's expected as the storm makes its push ashore. Forecast models show…
item.content:encoded:
Hurricane Isaias is moving toward landfall this evening along the Gulf Coast, with tropical storm-force winds already lashing the region, according to the National Hurricane Center. The NHC reported a 72 mph gust at Orange Beach, Alabama on Friday evening, giving a preview of what's expected as the storm makes its push ashore.

Forecast models show the system will make landfall sometime tonight. Residents across the northern Gulf Coast—including the Pensacola area—should prepare for heavy rain, gusty winds, and potential storm surge. The storm's exact track and intensity at landfall will determine which communities face the most significant impacts.

Local officials urge residents to monitor updates from the National Hurricane Center and follow guidance from emergency management agencies. If you haven't secured loose outdoor items, charged devices, or prepared supplies, now is the time to do so. Check on neighbors, finalize evacuation plans if needed, and stay weather-aware through landfall.

The northern Gulf Coast is already experiencing gusts approaching hurricane force. Orange Beach, Alabama has recorded wind…
item.content:encoded:
Hurricane Isaias is bearing down on the Pensacola area Friday evening, positioned about 60 miles south-southeast of the city and moving north at 17 mph with sustained winds of 115 mph, according to multiple weather reports.

The northern Gulf Coast is already experiencing gusts approaching hurricane force. Orange Beach, Alabama has recorded wind gusts up to 72 mph, with similar conditions reported offshore near Pensacola at 69 mph, according to weather observers tracking the storm.

With the hurricane on a northerly track at that speed, the Pensacola area faces the likelihood of significant impacts in the coming hours. Residents and visitors are urged to secure property, seek shelter, and follow guidance from local emergency management and the National Weather Service.

item.title: Tropical Cyclone Brings 51 mph Winds to NAS Pensacola
item.dc:creator: newsroom

The system moved through Escambia County with sustained tropical cyclone conditions. Residents in…
item.content:encoded:
A tropical cyclone brought gusty conditions to the Pensacola area Friday afternoon, with the National Escambia Mesonet station at NAS Pensacola recording a wind gust of 51 mph at 8:34 p.m. CDT, according to the IEMBOT Mob weather monitoring service.

The system moved through Escambia County with sustained tropical cyclone conditions. Residents in the area experienced the effects of the weather system through the evening hours.

No additional details about the storm's track, intensity, or expected impacts were immediately available. The National Weather Service in Mobile typically issues updated forecasts and warnings for tropical systems affecting Northwest Florida.
